title: Bloomberg This Weekend 8/22/2026
title_cn: 彭博社本周末 2026 年 8 月 22 日
summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Alexis Christoforous bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Former MI6 Chief Sir Richard Dearlove, American Whiskey Association President & CEO Michael Bilello, The Atlantic Contributing Writer and Columbia University Institute of Global Politics Distinguished Fellow Kim Ghattas, and Carleton College Professor of Economics and “Demographics and the Demand for Higher Education” Author Nathan Grawe. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
title_cn: 尖！彭博社针对冒险者的每周新闻测验
summary: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Alexis Christoforous, David Gura, and Christina Ruffini as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Colleges Face a Shrinking Student Pipeline
title_cn: 美国大学面临学生流失的问题
summary: US colleges are confronting a prolonged demographic squeeze as the number of high school graduates, after peaking in 2025, is projected to decline 13% through 2041, putting particular pressure on regional schools with limited endowments. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend is Carleton College Professor of Economics Nathan Grawe who explains that institutions are cutting programs, competing harder for students and emphasizing affordability and return on investment, while inflation-adjusted tuition at public four-year colleges has fallen 7% over the past decade. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sanctions Target Iran’s Weakened Regional Network
title_cn: 制裁针对伊朗薄弱的地区网络
summary: The US is preparing a new campaign of economic pressure on Iran after diplomacy and months of fighting failed to produce a durable settlement, with President Donald Trump warning countries against maintaining trade ties with Tehran. Atlantic writer and Columbia University Institute of Global Politics Distinguished Fellow Kim Ghattas is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that sanctions remain a blunt tool that will deepen hardship for ordinary Iranians, but Tehran’s weakened regional network and growing economic strain could make the latest pressure campaign different from those of the past 47 years. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Small Dogs, Big Demand as Dachshund Popularity Takes Off
title_cn: 随着腊肠犬的流行，小型犬的需求量很大
summary: Dachshunds are enjoying a global popularity boom, climbing to No. 5 in the American Kennel Club’s 2025 rankings as owners embrace their small size and outsized personalities.  The surge is supporting everything from breed meetups to dachshund cafes, even as owners contend with health concerns including intervertebral disc disease, which may affect roughly one in four dachshunds. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss all things Dachshund is Bloomberg News Bangkok Bureau Chief Randy Thanthong-Knight. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Study Shows AI Hitting Paychecks, Not Payrolls
title_cn: 研究表明人工智能影响的是薪水，而不是工资
summary: Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok says early labor-market data suggest AI’s first impact is appearing more in wages than employment. In a study of hundreds of occupations, Slok found that jobs with higher exposure to AI have seen weaker wage growth, while the employment effect remains relatively small. But the picture is still coming into focus: Slok says AI is also helping fuel record business formation, which could create new jobs and make the economy more dynamic. Former IBM HR chief Diane Gherson says companies are already deciding which work can be automated, which employees can be retrained and whether AI savings come through layoffs, slower hiring or reskilling.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Casinos Shift Focus From Gambling to Lure Gen Z With Sports, Dining

title: American Whiskey Pays Price for Canada Trade Rift
title_cn: 美国威士忌为加拿大贸易裂痕付出代价
summary: US spirits exports to Canada fell 70% from March through December 2025 after most provinces removed American alcohol from their shelves, while exports elsewhere rose 2.5%. American Whiskey Association President & CEO Michael Bilello is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says restoring market access is only the first challenge, American whiskey producers also need to rebuild demand among Canadian consumers after more than a year of trade tensions. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: MI6 Veteran Warns Against Politicizing Intelligence
title_cn: 军情六处资深人士警告不要将情报政治化
summary: Former Head of MI6 Sir Richard Dearlove joins Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the current state of the international intelligence community.  Dearlove says that UK-US intelligence cooperation remains close but expressed concern about politicization and personnel changes inside the CIA, an issue that has also drawn scrutiny amid broader changes across the US intelligence community. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Canada Pushes Back as US Trade Talks Collapse
title_cn: 美国贸易谈判破裂，加拿大予以反击
summary: Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that Canadians are frustrated but not necessarily surprised after last-minute US-Canada negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% US tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods and a dollar-for-dollar retaliation pledge from Ottawa. (Source: Bloomberg)

summary: Russia state-owned atomic energy company Rosatom is continuing to return employees to Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant, Interfax reported, citing the company’s Chief Executive Officer Alexey Likhachev.

title: Bond Market Tests Limits of Treasury Intervention
title_cn: 债券市场考验财政部干预的极限
summary: Joining Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg Radio host of "Masters in Business" Barry Ritholtz and he tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s bond-market moves may provide short-term relief but cannot override persistent inflation, rising debt and the forces setting long-term yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Luz Ding is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Chinese AI Models capabilities are approaching leading US models at lower cost. If adoption slows or cheaper Chinese open-source models gain traction, Big Tech may have to rethink the spending plans behind today’s AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Khosla Ventures Bets on AI’s Next Frontier: Science
title_cn: Khosla Ventures 押注人工智能的下一个前沿领域：科学
summary: Khosla Ventures is backing Discovery Loop, a new AI startup founded by former Google leaders including Jeff Dean that aims to dramatically accelerate scientific experimentation. Khosla Ventures Managing Director Samir Kaul explains why the firm quickly decided to invest, and why he believes the opportunity could be as profound as frontier AI models. He also discusses why soaring technology valuations are forcing venture investors to rethink what “seed stage” even means. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Meta Safety Trial Could Reveal What Zuckerberg, Others Knew
title_cn: 元安全试验可能揭示扎克伯格和其他人所知道的事情
summary: Meta is facing a landmark legal battle with 29 states accusing the company of deliberately designing its platforms to keep children hooked while misleading the public about their safety. George Washington University law professor Mary Anne Franks explains the state and federal claims, why the case has drawn comparisons to tobacco litigation, and why the biggest consequence may not be the potential financial penalty, but what internal documents reveal about what Meta knew and when. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Struggles to Absorb AI’s Debt Boom

summary: Broadcom is lining up another massive bet on AI. Bloomberg has learned the chipmaker is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt to help Anthropic and others secure chips and computing power. The deal highlights a bigger concern hanging over the AI trade: the cost of funding it all. Erica Klauer, Science and Technology Partners founder and CIO, discusses concerns around circular financing and why the AI buildout is so challenging. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

The maker of Claude could file publicly by the end of this month. The company raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation. Bloomberg's Shirin Ghaffary, who leads coverage of Anthropic, and Bloomberg's Liana Baker, who leads the deals team, join Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump’s New Midterm Pitch to Voters: Pretend I’m on Ballot
title_cn: 特朗普向选民的新中期宣传：假装我在选票上
summary: President Donald Trump tried out a new campaign message on Friday, telling voters in South Carolina to “pretend” he was on the ballot and turn out to back his hand-picked candidate, Senator Darline Graham, in a contentious Republican primary.

title: Lula Calls Trump to Resume Talks Over US Tariffs on Brazil
title_cn: 卢拉呼吁特朗普恢复有关美国对巴西关税的谈判
summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged Donald Trump to resume negotiations over US tariffs on Brazil during a Friday phone call, seeking to soothe relations with Washington ahead of the country’s October election.

title: US and Canada Race Against Clock to Hammer Out Trade Deal
title_cn: 美国和加拿大争分夺秒地敲定贸易协议
summary: US and Canadian negotiators haggled Friday over terms of a trade deal that would cut tariffs and retaliatory measures between the two major trading partners, with signs of optimism that a pact would be finalized before a midnight deadline in Washington.

title: Canada Nears Trump Trade Deal | Balance of Power 8/21/2026
title_cn: 加拿大接近特朗普贸易协议|权力平衡 2026 年 8 月 21 日
summary: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Canada's former Minister of International Trade Mary Ng, former National Security Advisor to President Trump John Bolton, CSIS Senior Nonresident Scholar Clayton Seigle, Rebelle Communications Founder & CEO Laura Fink, and Stonecourt Capital LP Rick Davis. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anwar’s One-Time Ally Turns Rival With New Malaysia Party
title_cn: 安瓦尔的曾经盟友与新马来西亚党成为竞争对手
summary: When Rafizi Ramli married in 2011, Malaysia’s future prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, hosted a celebration at his home. Fifteen years later, the former allies are now political rivals, with Rafizi setting the groundwork to one day sideline his former benefactor.

title: Leavitt Says She’ll Return to MAGA Inc. After White House
title_cn: 莱维特表示，离开白宫后她将重返 MAGA Inc.
summary: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said she will return to MAGA Inc., the president’s super political action committee, when she leaves her post later this month.

title: Seigle: Squeezing Iran Means Confronting China
title_cn: 塞格勒：挤压伊朗意味着对抗中国
summary: Senior Nonresident Scholar at the Center for Strategic and International Studies Clayton Seigle says a successful US economic pressure campaign against Iran would require confronting China, a major buyer of Iranian energy, potentially putting Washington's "fragile trade war détente" with Beijing at risk. Seigle says tougher pressure could also push energy prices higher if Iran retaliates against shipping or regional infrastructure, with US gasoline prices an important political concern ahead of the midterms. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'Hopeful' US. Canada Will Reach Deal: Fmr. Trade Official
title_cn: “充满希望”的美国。加拿大将达成协议：Fmr。贸易官员
summary: Former Canadian Trade Minister Mary Ng says she is hopeful the US and Canada can reach a trade agreement before Friday's deadline, pointing to positive signals from negotiators on both sides. Ng also says Canada should continue diversifying its trade relationships, pointing to opportunities across Asia including Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Indonesia. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's 'Balance of Power.' (Source: Bloomberg)
